title: Offline persistent subscriptions accumulate unbounded session message queues
source: Attacker-controlled cleanSession=false subscriber plus later PUBLISH messages to subscribed topics while the session is offline
driver: offline message count and payload bytes for a persistent clientIdentifier
retention: sessionMessages are removed only when the same clientIdentifier reconnects; no offline TTL, per-session message count, or byte quota found
bound: single message bounded by messageMaxSize; aggregate offline queue unbounded; clean sessions are cleared on close but persistent sessions are intentionally retained
impact: a default unauthenticated client can create a persistent subscription, disconnect, then enqueue many offline messages to itself or another persistent offline session. Static evidence is concrete but runtime OOM/unavailability was not measured.
static_trigger_shape: Client A CONNECT cleanSession=false, SUBSCRIBE dos/offline/#, DISCONNECT. Client B publishes many QoS1 messages with large payloads to dos/offline/{i}.
scope_notes: Process-memory offline queue, not DB/Redis persistence.
